## Compact Source Map — AMLO 2022 Chapter 5B

**Source**: GOV-003 — Comunicado No. 9, SHCP, "Informes sobre la Situación Económica, las Finanzas Públicas y la Deuda Pública al cuarto trimestre de 2022," 30 Jan 2023. Source role: **executive_official_report** (Ministry of Finance press release on Q4-2022 public finances and debt). Units: nominal pesos (MXN) and % of GDP unless noted; calendar year 2022 full-year unless a sub-period is given. All figures are ministry-reported, not independently audited; press-release language conflates policy intent with outcomes.

### Fiscal Aggregates (5B.3, 5B.10)
- Public debt: 49.4% of GDP at end-2022; lower than 2022 budget target and 2021 outturn by 1.6 and 1.4 pp of GDP, respectively. (block 1)
- Primary balance: **deficit** of 0.5% of GDP. Public deficit: **3.4%** of GDP. Public Sector Financial Requirements (RFSP): **4.4%** of GDP. (block 5)
- Combined fiscal buffers: MXN-equivalent 262 billion USD — international reserves, IMF Flexible Credit Line, Fed swap line, stabilization funds. (block 5)
- Debt operations Oct–Dec 2022: 7 Oct buyback MXN 68,017m (2023–2046) paired with MXN 48,596m long-bond sale; 30 Nov Bondes G (1y/2y/3y) MXN 7,090m / 2,660m / 250m; 7 Dec new Bono M May-2033 MXN 12,500m at 7.5% coupon; 8 Dec 2033/2053 Bono M placement MXN 50,863m with 2029–2047 buyback. (block 6)
- Refinancing claim: 2023 + two subsequent years debt-pressures reduced on average 73% via buybacks, freeing USD 3bn for next administration. (block 6, ministry claim — forward-looking)
- Sovereign ratings: investment grade + stable outlook from all 8 rating agencies (per ministry); 21 international recognitions for debt management in this administration. (block 6, ministry claim)

### Revenue (5B.3, 5B.7, 5B.9)
- Total public revenues 2022: MXN 6.595 trillion, MXN 422bn above program; +2.5% vs 2021 (two consecutive years of growth). (block 4)
- Federal government got MXN 632bn above program, of which MXN 397bn reflects lower-than-programmed IEPS fuel excise collection (i.e., a subsidy cost, not a revenue gain — composition effect). (block 4)
- Oil revenues: MXN 1.482 trillion = 5.2% of GDP, highest since 2014; +18.7% real annual vs 2021 (high oil-price-driven, ministry-stated cause). (block 4)
- Tax revenues ex-fuel-IEPS: 13.6% of GDP (record high in available series); +7.8% real annual, fastest since 2016. (block 4)
- ISR (income tax): MXN 2.270 trillion = 8.0% of GDP (record); +11% real annual, fastest since 2016; ministry attributes to real-wage gains. (block 4)
- IVA (VAT): MXN 1.222 trillion = 4.3% of GDP, vs historical average 3.9%; ministry attributes to consumption strength. (block 4)

### Expenditure (5B.1, 5B.6, 5B.8)
- Public spending 2022: MXN 7.569 trillion = 26.5% of GDP; +4.1% real annual (three consecutive years of real growth). (block 5)
- Social protection spending: +8.7% real annual; 5.3% of GDP (record high). (block 5)
- Physical investment: +25.2% (highest since 2009); 3.3% of GDP (highest since 2016). (block 5)
- Federal transfers to states/municipalities: highest in available record; +7.3% real annual. (block 5)

### Macro Context (5B.9, 5B.10)
- GDP growth: 2.9% YoY to Nov-2022 (better than analyst expectations, ministry-stated). (block 2)
- Unemployment: 2.8% total / 2.5% women (lowest in 17 years per ministry); 2022 average 3.3%. Job creation: 2.4m positions; 753k new IMSS affiliates (third-highest since 1997, mostly permanent). Real average wage: +2.7% annual. (blocks 2–3)
- Private consumption: +7.1% YoY to Oct-2022 vs 2.7% historical average; services consumption recovered to pre-pandemic level. (blocks 2–3)
- Gross fixed investment: +5.5% YoY to Oct-2022 vs 1.6% historical; machinery/equipment +12.2% vs 5.0% historical. (block 3)
- Trade: USD 1.2 trillion record; new FDI inflows USD 14bn (second-highest after 2013); 2022 total FDI USD 32bn to Q3 (highest since 2013); net capital outflows USD 19bn lower than 2021. (blocks 2–3)
- 2023 global growth expected ~2.1%; ministry cites China reopening and lower commodity prices. (block 2, forecast)
- Inflationary pressures: ministry states supply-chain disruptions and transport costs diminished in 2022, easing price pressures. (block 2)

### Source Limitations & Caveats
- **Author/source role**: SHCP press release — institutional self-reporting; explicit gob.mx boilerplate states legality/accuracy is the providing agency's responsibility. (block 7)
- **No independent audit, preliminary-vs-final status, or accounting-basis (cash vs accrual, nominal vs real) statement** appears in the extract; all figures are ministry-reported and unaudited here.
- **Program-vs-outturn gaps**: "above program" is the relevant comparison basis; the report does not present revised program or methodology notes within the extract.
- **Composition risk in revenue claim**: the MXN 632bn above-program figure includes a MXN 397bn IEPS-fuel revenue shortfall (subsidy), partially offsetting the headline beat — the extract presents them in sequence, not netted.
- **Oil-revenue durability**: 18.7% real growth explicitly tied to "altos precios del petróleo" — an external commodity-price effect, not a structural revenue change.
- **Forward-looking statements** (refinancing plan, 2023 growth, China reopening) are ministry projections, not outturns.
- **Definition note**: "RFSP" (Public Sector Financial Requirements, 4.4%) is broader than the headline public deficit (3.4%) — both retained because the report does both.
- **Material not in extract**: detailed sectoral/regional incidence, fiscal-rule compliance assessment, arrears, off-budget items, auditor opinion — absent from this chunk and not asserted.

**Reopen-later flags for stronger model**: (i) net the IEPS-fuel offset against revenue beat; (ii) cross-check RFSP definition vs headline deficit against independent SHCP statistics at presto.hacienda.gob.mx/EstoporLayout/estadisticas.jsp (block 7 URL); (iii) test whether the +25.2% investment growth and 3.3% of GDP level are consistent with INEGI outturns once published; (iv) verify rating-agency statements against each agency's own bulletin (block 6 ministry framing only); (v) check whether the "73% pressure reduction" refers to scheduled maturities or a different metric.
